name: Low BTC-correlation sleeve with an exponentially weighted correlation (60-day half-life), rank-weighted, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. lambda = 0.5^(1/halfLife); u_j = lambda^j for j = 0..span-1 (j = 0 is the latest bar). For every symbol with L >= need: r_s[j] = ret(b_s, e-j). Weighted mean mu_s = sum_j u_j r_s[j] / sum_j u_j; weighted cov c = sum_j u_j (r_s[j]-mu_s)(r_B[j]-mu_B) / sum_j u_j with B = BTCUSDT; weighted var likewise; corr_s = c/sqrt(v_s v_B); BTCUSDT corr = 1. n = scored symbols; if n < minNames (or BTCUSDT has L < need) return ew. Rank weights: sort descending by corr (position 1 = highest corr); weight of position q = q/T with T = n(n+1)/2, so the lowest-correlation name gets the largest weight. Monthly rebalance, long-only.
rationale: redteam-04's fixed 90-day correlation gives every day equal say and drops days abruptly; an exponentially weighted estimate tracks recent co-movement smoothly, which is the property the forward window rewarded.
source: campaign-1022/REPORT.md section 4 idea 1; extends c1022-redteam-04 (Frazzini & Pedersen 2014 JFE); RiskMetrics Technical Document 1996 (EWMA covariance)

name: Low BTC-correlation sleeve only while the EW alt index is below its 200-day SMA, BTC otherwise
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. EW alt index: alts = symbols other than BTCUSDT with L >= idxNeed (if fewer than 4, return ew); m_k = mean over alts of ret(b,k) for k = e-smaDays+1..e; level Lv_{e-smaDays} = 1, Lv_k = Lv_{k-1}*(1+m_k); SMA = mean of Lv_k over k = e-smaDays+1..e; riskOff = Lv_e < SMA. If riskOff: corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-window+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1); a symbol with L < need is skipped; n = number of scored symbols; if n < minNames return ew. Rank weights: sort descending by corr (position 1 = highest corr); weight of position q = q/T with T = n(n+1)/2, so the lowest-correlation name gets the largest weight. If not riskOff: return {BTCUSDT: 1}. If BTCUSDT has L < need return ew. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: The forward window where cluster A held up was one where alts lagged BTC; this asks whether the low-correlation tilt is only worth holding in that regime, with plain BTC the alternative rather than cash.

name: Low BTC-correlation picks (bottom half) sized by inverse realised volatility, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-window+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1); a symbol with L < need is skipped; n = number of scored symbols; if n < minNames return ew. Sort ascending by corr; H = the floor(selectFrac*n) lowest-correlation symbols. sigma_s = sample standard deviation of ret(b_s,k) over the same window. w_s = (1/sigma_s) / sum over H of (1/sigma); weights sum to 1. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: Rank and equal weights let the most volatile low-correlation coin dominate the sleeve's risk; inverse-vol sizing tests whether the effect survives when each pick contributes similar risk (risk parity inside the factor).

name: Low BTC-correlation sleeve, bottom half, with a 70th-percentile hold buffer, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-window+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1); a symbol with L < need is skipped; n = number of scored symbols; if n < minNames return ew. Rank ascending by corr; percentile p_s = (position-1)/(n-1). Hold set H in ctx.state (starts empty): drop s from H if it is unscored or p_s > holdPct; then add symbols in ascending corr order (skipping ones already in H) until |H| = ceil(selectPct*n). Equal weight over H. If n < minNames: reset H to empty and return ew. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: redteam-03 applied this buffer to beta against the EW index; redteam-04 (correlation, no buffer) was the strongest forward survivor, so the question is whether the correlation version keeps its edge once turnover on small rank changes is removed.

name: Alt/BTC ratio above its 50-day SMA, restricted to the 9 alts with the lowest 90-day BTC beta (A x B)
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. BTC = BTCUSDT; if BTC has L < need return {}. Sleeve set S is refreshed on the first rank call of each UTC calendar month (ctx.state.month = year*12+month) and kept in ctx.state: among alts with L >= need, beta_s = cov(ret_s, ret_BTC)/var(ret_BTC) over k = e-betaWindow+1..e (sample); S = the nLow lowest-beta alts (all qualifying alts if fewer than nLow). Then retail-41's rule on S only: btcUp = BTC close_e > SMA(btcSma) of BTC close; if not btcUp return {}; holders = alts in S whose R_0 > mean of R_m (m = 0..ratioSma-1, R_m = alt close/BTC close); if no holders return {BTCUSDT: 1}; else equal weight over holders. Daily, long-only.
rationale: Clusters A and B both survived; applying B's relative-strength trigger only inside A's low-beta set asks whether the alt/BTC breakout edge comes from the wild high-beta names (survivorship/beta exposure) or holds in the calmer half too.

name: Crypto momentum consensus (14/21/28) with the most recent week removed from every horizon, weekly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Reading of the idea (fixed before code): redteam-10's horizons are 14/21/28, so there is no 1-week horizon to delete; the 1-week removal is applied as a skip of the most recent 7 days inside each horizon, a falsification test of redteam-11's -25% neighbour (where the skipped week hurt). rows = symbols with L >= need; n = rows; if n < minNames return ew. For each h in horizons: score_h(s) = b[e-skip].close/b[e-h].close-1; top_h = the ceil(n/2) highest. H = intersection of top_h over all h. If |H| < minHold return {} (cash, as redteam-10). Equal weight over H. Weekly, long-only.
rationale: If the recent week carries the crypto momentum signal (redteam-11's neighbour result), removing it from a consensus that was forward-positive should make it worse; if the consensus survives, the signal lives in weeks 2-4 and the one-week skip is harmless.

name: Vol-neutralised 90-day momentum (top 20%) with a 50% hold buffer, daily
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. As mlq-feature-neutral-momentum: rows = symbols with L >= lookback+2; mom = b[e].close/b[e-lookback].close-1; vol = sqrt(mean of ret^2 over k = e-lookback+1..e); cross-sectional OLS mom = a + b*vol, resid = mom - (a + b*vol). M = rows; if M < minRows: reset ctx.state.H to empty and return {}. Sort descending by resid -> rank 1..M. K = max(1, round(topFrac*M)); B = ceil(bufferFrac*M). keep = names in ctx.state.H whose rank <= B; then add ranked names not in keep from rank 1 upward until |keep| = K; if |keep| > K keep the K best-ranked. ctx.state.H = keep; equal weight over keep. Daily, long-only. No other change from the parent.
rationale: mlq was forward-positive at +40.7pp with daily top-20% churn; mom-buffer showed a 50% buffer kept the momentum edge with far less trading, so this is the single-change cost-aware version of the vol-neutral rule.
source: campaign-1022/REPORT.md section 4 idea 11; extends mlq-feature-neutral-momentum and r27-crypto-mom-buffer; Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen 2013 JF; Novy-Marx & Velikov 2016 RFS

name: Rank-weighted 3-week momentum with a BTC volume-share veto (cash when BTC's 7-day share is above its 60-day mean), weekly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Veto (crypto-45's signal): if BTCUSDT has L < lWin return {}. For each of the last lWin BTC bar times T: dollar volume dv_s = close*volume of the bar with time T for every symbol in the view that has it; share_T = dv_BTC / sum_s dv_s. veto = mean(share over the last sWin times) > mean(share over all lWin times). If veto: return {} (cash). Else redteam-13's sleeve: rows = symbols with L >= need, score = b[e].close/b[e-lookback].close-1; if rows < minNames return ew; sort descending; position q = 1 is the best; weight = (n-q+1)/T, T = n(n+1)/2. Weekly, long-only.
rationale: crypto-45 lost as a picker (one coin carried it) but its signal, rising BTC turnover share, is a plausible flight-to-BTC marker; used only as an on/off gate on a forward-positive momentum sleeve it is a cleaner test of the signal.

rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. elig = symbols with L > 260 (acad-61's guard); N = |elig|; if N < minNames return ew. vol_s = sample std of ret(b,e-m), m = 0..volBars-1. HV = the floor(highVolFrac*N) highest-vol names. mom_s = b[e-skip].close/b[e-form].close-1 on HV; sleeve = the k = floor(topFrac*N) highest (k < 3 -> return ew). Spread series s_j = mean over sleeve of ret(b,e-j) - mean over elig of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..spreadWindow-1; sd = sample std of s * sqrt(252); w = sd > 0 ? min(1, target/sd) : 1. Weights: (1-w)/N on every elig name plus w/k on each sleeve name. Monthly, long-only.

rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. elig = symbols with L >= need; M = |elig|; if M < minNames return ew. N = max(minHoldings, round(fraction*M)). Sleeve 1 (momentum): mom_s = b[e-skip].close/b[e-form].close-1; w1 = 1/N on the N highest. Sleeve 2 (downside beta): Downside beta (r25-downside-beta-high construction, e = L-1): elig = symbols with L >= need; market m_j = mean over elig of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..window-1; down = {j: m_j < 0}; if |down| < minDown return ew; beta_s = cov(ret_s, m) over down days / var(m) over down days (sums over the down set, same centring as the parent module). if the downside-beta sleeve is unavailable (|down| < minDown) w2 = 1/M on every elig; else w2 = 1/N on the N highest beta_s. Final weight w_s = 0.5*w1_s + 0.5*w2_s (a name in both sleeves gets both halves). Monthly, long-only.
rationale: Clusters C and D are the two equity themes that held up forward and they load on different things (past return vs down-market sensitivity); a fixed 50/50 book asks whether they diversify or are one bet in disguise.

name: High downside beta with the sleeve volatility matched to the EW universe, exposure check (e) as a hard gate (wide US stocks)
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Downside beta (r25-downside-beta-high construction, e = L-1): elig = symbols with L >= need; market m_j = mean over elig of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..window-1; down = {j: m_j < 0}; if |down| < minDown return ew; beta_s = cov(ret_s, m) over down days / var(m) over down days (sums over the down set, same centring as the parent module). M = |elig|; if M < minNames return ew. N = max(minHoldings, round(fraction*M)); sleeve = the N highest beta_s. sigma_S = sample std over j = 0..volWindow-1 of (mean over sleeve of ret(b,e-j)); sigma_M = same for elig; w = sigma_S > 0 ? min(1, sigma_M/sigma_S) : 1. Weights: w/N on each sleeve name plus (1-w)/M on every elig name (gross exposure always 1, sleeve risk matched to the benchmark's by construction). Monthly, long-only. Gate (declared now, applied at retest): this id counts as ahead only if the retest exposure check (e) passes (strategy CAGR > exposure x B&H CAGR and strategy Sharpe > B&H Sharpe); a check-(e) fail is a FAIL for this id regardless of excess.
rationale: r25-downside-beta-high had the lowest forward p in the retest (0.027) but failed check (e), meaning part of its edge was simply more risk; matching the sleeve's realised volatility to the benchmark's removes that explanation before the test is run.
source: campaign-1022/REPORT.md section 4 idea 19; extends r25-downside-beta-high; Ang, Chen & Xing 2006 RFS (downside risk); Barroso & Santa-Clara 2015 JFE (volatility scaling)

name: Lowest VIX-beta stocks from weekly innovations, weekly rebalance (40 large caps)
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Weekly rank calls. v = ctx.macro('VIX') (latest known by the rebalance close). ctx.state.hist = list of {v, close: {s: b[e].close for every symbol in the view}} appended once per call, capped at maxHist entries (drop the oldest). For symbol s: over the last `weeks`+1 consecutive entries, pairs (dV_j = v_j - v_{j-1}, r_j = close_j/close_{j-1}-1) where both v values are finite and s has a close in both entries; require exactly `weeks` pairs else skip s. beta_s = OLS slope of r on dV. Hold the `top` lowest beta_s, 1/top each (ties by name); fewer than `top` scored -> return {}. Weekly, long-only. Differences from s29-us-vix-beta fixed a priori: innovations and returns are weekly not daily, beta is re-estimated every week, and the book is rebalanced weekly (the parent drifted daily, 402 decisions in 402 forward days).
rationale: vix-beta's +45pp forward came with daily drift-restoring trades; the Ang et al. result is about exposure to volatility innovations, which should survive weekly measurement and rebalance if it is more than churn.
source: campaign-1022/REPORT.md section 4 idea 20; extends s29-us-vix-beta; Ang, Hodrick, Xing & Zhang 2006 JF (cross-section of volatility and expected returns)

name: High downside beta sorted inside the high-volatility half only (wide US stocks), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Downside beta (r25-downside-beta-high construction, e = L-1): elig = symbols with L >= need; market m_j = mean over elig of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..window-1; down = {j: m_j < 0}; if |down| < minDown return ew; beta_s = cov(ret_s, m) over down days / var(m) over down days (sums over the down set, same centring as the parent module). M = |elig|; if M < minNames return ew. vol_s = sample std of ret(b,e-m), m = 0..volBars-1; HV = the floor(highVolFrac*M) highest-vol names. N = max(minHoldings, round(fraction*M)) (20% of the full count, as acad-61); hold the N highest beta_s within HV, 1/N each. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: acad-61 showed momentum is stronger among high-volatility names; if downside beta is a priced risk the same cut should sharpen it, and if the D-cluster edge was only a volatility tilt the cut will show nothing beyond acad-61's universe.
source: campaign-1022/REPORT.md section 4 idea 21; extends r25-downside-beta-high and c1022-acad-61; Ang, Chen & Xing 2006 RFS; Bandarchuk & Hilscher 2013 JFM

name: Top 5 of 20 ETFs by 12-1 momentum with a 20% volatility-managed overlay (remainder in AGG/IEF), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. scored = symbols with L >= need, score = b[e-skip].close/b[e-lookback].close-1; if fewer than minNames return ew. picks = the `top` highest. Sleeve daily return p_j = mean over picks of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..volWindow-1; var = sample variance of p * 252; w = var > 0 ? min(1, targetVar/var) : 1. Weights: w/top on each pick. Remainder 1-w goes to AGG if AGG is in the view and not a pick, else to IEF if in the view and not a pick, else stays cash. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: etf20-xsmom was a clean-battery forward survivor and qqq-agg-volmanaged was forward-positive but untestable on the drop leg; the Moreira-Muir overlay on a 20-asset momentum book tests the sizing rule where every asset can be removed.
source: campaign-1022/REPORT.md section 4 idea 23; extends r27-etf20-xsmom and r25-qqq-agg-volmanaged; Moreira & Muir 2017 JF (volatility-managed portfolios); Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen 2013 JF

name: Dual momentum across five risk ETFs (QQQ, DIA, GLD, DBC, VNQ) versus four safe ETFs (AGG, IEF, TLT, SHY), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. R(s) = b[e].close/b[e-lookback].close-1 for every symbol in the view with L >= need (others unscored). bestRisk = the scored risk symbol with the highest R (ties by name); bestSafe = the scored safe symbol with the highest R. If bestRisk exists and R(bestRisk) > 0 and (bestSafe is absent or R(bestRisk) > R(bestSafe)): return {bestRisk: 1}. Else if bestSafe exists: return {bestSafe: 1}. Else return ew. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: Every 2-3 asset dual-momentum switcher was forward-positive (+15 to +18pp) but could not be battery-tested; the same absolute-plus-relative rule over nine assets keeps the logic and gives the drop leg something to remove.
source: campaign-1022/REPORT.md section 4 idea 24; extends r25-qqq-agg-dualmom and r27-qqq-gld-agg-dualmom; Antonacci 2014 'Dual Momentum Investing'; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012 JFE
